seal.statement: finalizeTestRun in scripts/run-test-files.js read each test's whole stdout AND stderr into strings. On 2026-09-17 test/integration/message-group-multi-join-formation.integration.test.js wrote 608,651,868 bytes under lane contention, past V8's string cap, so readFileSync threw ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG and killed the runner mid-lane: 220 of 262 exclusive files had passed and their results died with it - an unhandled crash, not a test failure. The same unbounded text was also echoed to the console for any failed file, so a red half-gigabyte output would have been printed in full into the gate log. The reader is now bounded: readBoundedOutput streams the file in 1 MiB chunks, feeds every byte to the tap parser (a streaming parser, so the verdict is unchanged), offers every complete line so the top-level time tail is found however deep it lies, and keeps only the first and last 64 KiB with an elision naming the file that holds the rest. Measured on a 575 MB fixture: readFileSync still throws, the bounded reader takes 0.7 s at constant memory and reports the same single passing assertion. The result also carries outputBytes and stderrBytes, so a runaway output is visible rather than merely survivable.

text: readBoundedOutput streams each output in 1 MiB chunks: every byte goes to the tap parser through a new createTapAnalysis sink (analyzeTapOutput keeps its string signature on top of it), complete lines are offered so the top-level time tail is found line-wise, and only the first and last 64 KiB are kept with an elision naming the file. finalizeTestRun uses it for stdout and stderr and reports outputBytes/stderrBytes. Witnessed with a 520 MiB fixture that readFileSync still cannot hold, a 2 MiB line spanning chunk boundaries, an edge-keeping case and a small verbatim case; reverting to a whole-file read turns three of them red

round 1 REJECT (2 blocking): (1) , the whole-line accumulator, is just another unbounded string - a newline-free output past the cap throws RangeError out of finalizeTestRun and dies uncaught in runTestFile's close handler, killing the lane exactly as readFileSync did, and OOM-aborts under a 256 MB heap; the constraint no-lane-dies-for-output was false as written. (2) chars-versus-bytes: head/tail lengths are UTF-16 counts compared with byte counts, so any non-ASCII output is duplicated by (bytes - chars) characters at the join - proven on a real 95,285-byte artifact in this repository - and a heavy-multibyte truncated file yields the content twice plus a false elided count. Verdict equivalence itself HELD across 20 TAP shapes including nested subtests, bailout, CRLF and a character straddling the chunk seam; no fd leak in any error path; memory bounded for line-structured output. Non-blocking: witness gaps for the EOF flush, the 64-128 KiB band and the Buffer-vs-string seam; CR-anchored time lines; an absolute path in the elision reaching deterministic-guard-report; readLastResult's whole-file read kept out of scope.

round 1 repair went deeper than the report: capping the reader is not enough because tap-parser itself accumulates (this.buffer += chunk) until a line ends, so a newline-free 520 MiB output overflows INSIDE the parser however the file is read - reproduced against the streamed version. The bound is now per line and in bytes: each line's first 1 MiB reaches the parser, the terminator always does, the runaway tail is dropped and counted in ; the excerpt is built from Buffers so any file within the two edges is byte-for-byte verbatim whatever its encoding; lines end at LF or CR as the /^# time=/m anchor did; the elision names a repository-relative path. Measured end to end: a 545 MB newline-free spew leaves the lane alive with the passing file's result intact and the spewer reported as an ordinary failure, at a 256 MB heap too. Witnesses grew from 4 to 10 receipts and cover every mutation the verifier found green

follow-up (not this quest): readLastResult in scripts/run-classified-test-files.js still reads a whole .tap as a string for the LPT ordering hint; its try/catch makes an oversized file safe (the file ranks unknown), so the cost is a lost duration hint, not a crash. It could use readBoundedOutput's tail once this lands.

correction to the two entries above, whose backticked words were eaten by the shell before they reached the log: the verification's finding (1) names the whole-line accumulator variable "pending", and the repair note says the runaway tail of a line is counted in the returned field "dropped". Nothing else in either entry changed.

round 2 REJECT (1 blocking): the per-line analysis cap can change a verdict, including red to green SILENTLY - ok 1 - runaway description followed by # SKIP loses the skip past the cap and reads as a plain pass, where the whole-string analysis reported not-ok. Two related shapes reclassify without flipping (a TODO past the cap, a quoted YAML scalar cut mid-quote). Everything else verified fixed and re-proved independently: the 545 MB newline-free lane survives at both heaps with the green file's result intact and 131 KB echoed instead of 545 MB; the round-1 multibyte artifact in this repository now reads verbatim with surplus 0; the 20-sample equivalence corpus has zero mismatches including CR anchoring; ten mutations all red, including the three that were green in round 1; dropped accounting exact across seven shapes; the stderr path accumulates nothing; the byte stream handed to the parser is byte-identical to the file whenever no line exceeds the cap (300-file randomized sweep). Non-blocking: replacement characters at a multibyte excerpt edge, displayPath resolving against process.cwd rather than options.cwd.

round 2 repair: finalizeTestRun computed the dropped count and threw it away. A file whose output could not be analysed whole is now FAILED, with a reason naming how many bytes of how many went unanalysed, and the count is carried on the result as outputDropped. That closes the silent-green class whatever the cut removed, rather than chasing directives; the constraint now says the verdict is preserved OR the file is failed. Witnessed by a fixture whose passing line hides its SKIP past the bound (red without the reason, green with it) and by an ordinary file that drops nothing

round 3 APPROVE: failing on incomplete analysis rather than enumerating directive shapes is the right altitude - all three round-2 shapes now come back failed through the real runner, and for the silent-green one the dropped reason is the ONLY thing making it red (the analysis alone still reports assertions=1 skips=0 parserOk=true). Measured headroom: across all 2,577 tap and stderr artifacts in this repository the longest single line is 9,886 bytes, about 106x under the bound, so nothing regresses today; a legitimate green file with a >1 MiB single line does now fail, which is the declared contract, loud and named, and the remedy is the constant rather than narrowing the rule. Accounting exact (dropped 524,329 of a 1,572,926-byte file, consumed + dropped == bytes in every shape); equivalence corpus 20/20 with zero mismatches; byte-identity invariant proven over a 300-file randomized sweep; 13 mutations applied, 12 red at review time; no fd leaks; stderr structurally drops nothing. Non-blocking: the reason's numbers were unpinned (mutation m), retryFailedOnce gains a new entry path for runaway-output files, and the previously recorded U+FFFD edge cuts and displayPath cwd observations stand.

round 3 follow-up: the reason's two numbers are pinned by an exact-string assertion (swapping them now turns the witness red, closing the verifier's mutation m), and the measured real-world maximum line of 9,886 bytes is recorded beside OUTPUT_LINE_ANALYSIS_BYTES with the instruction to raise the constant rather than narrow the rule if a legitimate file ever exceeds it

Altitude check. Three rounds, three defects, each deeper than the last: a whole-file read, then a whole-line accumulator that was the same bug in a new place, then the tap parser's own buffering, then a capped line that could flip a verdict. The altitude was right only from round 2 on, when the question changed from 'how do I read this file safely' to 'what may the parser be shown, and what must I refuse to judge'. The lesson worth keeping is the last one: when an analysis cannot be complete, fail the subject rather than report a verdict from the part you did see - a rule keyed on the content of the cut would have closed only the shapes we thought of. Scope stayed correct throughout: readLastResult's whole-file read in the classified runner is safe behind its try/catch and remains a recorded follow-up rather than a widening of this quest.
